corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science papers on large language models, the corpus reveals a dispersed but coherent focus on AI as a research tool, health information governance, education and literacy, societal risk and fairness, and culture/heritage design. Findings emphasize methodological innovation, cautious adoption, user trust, and the need for transparent governance and ethical considerations as AI permeates research, learning, and public discourse.

themes.name: AI as methodological innovator and research tool
themes.description: Papers show LLMs and multi-agent systems enabling novel social-science methods, including coding, analysis, data extraction, cross-domain transfer, and governance framing.

themes.name: Health information, care, and governance with AI
themes.description: Research examines AI-generated health misinformation, clinician decision support, patient education, and equity-focused governance of digital health AI.

themes.name: AI in education and AI literacy
themes.description: Papers explore AI adoption in classrooms and universities, AI-assisted learning, and initiatives to build AI literacy across learners and age groups.

themes.name: Fairness, bias, safety, and societal risks of LLM deployment
themes.description: Work investigates fairness across user groups, fallibility under misinformation pressure, deepfake warnings, and normative standards for responsible AI.

themes.name: Culture, heritage, and design with AI
themes.description: Digital humanities and design pedagogy leverage AI for heritage reconstruction, sense-of-place analysis, and culturally grounded aesthetic learning.

emergingKeywords: Public policy and governance of LLMs
